trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out left, down or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
I can't rule out right or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to number 4, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6). So my guess (right from cell (3,3)) was wrong, so the line must go up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6); going left leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try down.
I can't rule out down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6). So the line goes left.
Going left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 3. So my guess (down from cell (5,4)) was wrong, so the line must go left.
Going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6). So the line goes up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (down from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go up.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6). So the line goes up.
Going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,6). So the line goes through the portal to (6,1).
The line must go up: right is number 9, which comes later.
Going right would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes up.
The line must go up: right is number 10, which comes later.
Going right would cut off the top edge (12 cells). So the line goes up.
Going up would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going right would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going down would cut off the top-right corner (6 cells). So the line goes right.
Going down would cut off the top-right corner (4 cells). So the line goes right.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going left would wall in number 10, the last number; going down would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going down would cut off the bottom-left corner (4 cells). So the line goes right.
Cell (5,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!

Tried 96 futures: 54% survive going right (best covers 47%); up 8%; left 0%.
Jackpot! A future covers the whole board. Cashing in!
